data.narrative:
eleQtron is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised €50M+ to date. The target operates within a sector encompassing 11 comparable entities: 3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation approach given data constraints. Using total capital raised (€50M) as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of €100M. Peer-median analysis was not executable due to insufficient narrow comparables at matching stage and valuation tier within quantum computing—while 6 same-sector peers exist, none satisfied the three-datapoint minimum threshold when filtered by stage, timing, and valuation proximity. Broad-sector medians were rejected to avoid false precision.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €85M–€115M, centered at €100M. This represents the stage-progression result with a ±15% confidence envelope. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.0x multiplier for this specific subsector, the absence of directly comparable Series A-stage quantum hardware companies, and variability in financing terms across the peer set. Further substantiation would require either tighter peer clustering or access to recent Series A transaction data in quantum computing.
